trust_decision.summary: Whether a file counts as an image, and therefore how it is stored and served, is decided by its filename extension alone: the import archive selects image files by extension, the import handler stores them unchecked, and the storage layer derives the served Content-Type from that same extension; nothing on the import path inspects contents or sanitizes SVG.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names content imports, and this is the import handler that normalises and stores every archived file whose name carries an image extension, with no content check and no SVG sanitization.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /ghost/api/admin/db/media/inline/ and remote media inlining during POST /ghost/api/admin/posts/upload/
shared helper required by the importer, upload middleware, media inliner and oembed service
shared helper (SVG sanitizer extracted from the upload middleware)
process boot (restrictImageDecoders applied before any image is processed)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The media inliner is a different feature in a different service directory: it only re-hosts images that already-published posts link to, and its storage picker looks like adapter selection rather than image validation, so a solver can argue the advisory's 'content imports' do not cover it (and that storeMediaLocally only has a buffer, not an archive file, so the import fix cannot apply).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SVG (and .svgz) uploads must keep being accepted after sanitizing - file-type cannot detect text-based SVG, so a uniform 'contents must be a detected image format' rule rejects every SVG; the icon upload validator also deliberately skips its 60x60 minimum-dimension rule for SVG.

O6_input_shapes: file path on disk (string) versus in-memory buffer (Uint8Array)
contents of an allowed format stored under a different image extension (PNG bytes named .jpg)
SVG content under a non-SVG name (rasterize instead of trusting the name)
gzipped SVG (.svgz) versus plain SVG text
extensions configured as allowed that are not image types at all (.pdf, .bmp, .ico in the table-less path)
configured content types with different case/whitespace and non-image types (text/html, text/xml, application/pdf)
same extension string in a differently-cased allowlist

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public GET /content/images/size/:dimension[/format/:format]/<path>: it reads the stored original, hands its bytes to sharp via imageTransform.resizeFromBuffer and writes the result back into image storage under a name/extension taken from the request URL, with no content allowlist and no SVG sanitization (image-transform returns the original bytes when they are smaller than the converted ones).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a cache/derivative route, not an upload: anything it reads was already stored through a validated path, unsupported types redirect to the original, and the advisory is about archive imports.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: frontend web middleware, two directories from the importer; unauthenticated route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth content-file handler for another asset type (e.g. avatars, social/OG images) declared in the same createContentFileHandlers array.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Handlers are a declarative list of type/extensions/directories tied to uploads config keys, so a maintainer adding an asset type adds a handler and an importer here without touching the image handler's validation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new uploads type (e.g. uploads.avatars) appended to the storage-picker chain that also resolves to an image storage adapter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The chain is a flat if/else over uploads config keys and image-served types (images, thumbnails, icons in the fix) are added by config, not by a shared predicate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new admin upload route registered with validation({type: 'images'}) but with its own content handling (like media/thumbnail/upload).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every upload route re-declares its middleware stack, so a new endpoint can reuse the image validation while bypassing a fix applied only to the paths the report named.

O9_family: Unrestricted upload of a dangerous file type leading to stored XSS (image/SVG content trusted by name; CWE-434 / CWE-79)
